_client_secret: Needed to stay logged in. Twitch only lets a Public client refresh without one; the console defaults to Confidential. Leave it out and the bot must be re-authorised about every 4 hours.
_fact_source: 'sources' (default): find real facts on Wikipedia/web, then rewrite them. 'llm': skip retrieval and ask the model for facts from its own knowledge - simpler and often better for famous places, but nothing is verified, so it can invent.
_llm_options: The three llm_* fields above are set for OpenRouter (recommended for adult-aligned facts). Other providers: Groq -> key 'gsk_...', base 'https://api.groq.com/openai/v1', model 'openai/gpt-oss-120b'. Local Ollama -> key '' (empty), base 'http://localhost:11434/v1', model 'llama3.1:8b'. Other OpenRouter models: 'sao10k/l3.3-euryale-70b' (edgiest), 'cognitivecomputations/dolphin-mistral-24b-venice-edition' (uncensored), 'mistralai/mistral-nemo' (cheapest).
_llm_fallback: The bot's second LLM provider: when the llm_* provider above is rate-limited (Groq's free tier 429s mid-stream), chat replies, sourced answers and fact writing switch to this provider until the window clears, and both are warmed at startup. FREE OpenRouter setup: key 'sk-or-...' (create one at openrouter.ai/keys, no card needed), base 'https://openrouter.ai/api/v1' (the default when left empty), model a slug ending in ':free'. Free slugs are shared-capacity, rotate, and can fail even while their model page is up, so recheck openrouter.ai/models instead of copying a hard-coded recommendation. Use a paid non-:free slug or local Ollama when the fallback must be dependable. Free-tier limits: 20 requests/minute, 50/day on a fresh account (raised to 1000/day forever by any one-time $10 credit purchase) - plenty for a fallback that carries requests only while Groq clears. A local Ollama fallback also works: key '', base 'http://localhost:11434/v1', model 'qwen3:4b' - no key, no limits, no rotation. Leave llm_fallback_model empty (the default) to keep a single provider. Startup first prints fallback READY, OFF or MISCONFIGURED for the config, then the live warm-up prints fallback READY only after an answer or fallback NOT READY with the provider's real error.
_chat_ai: The bot's own voice in chat. When enabled: !ask anything gets a persona answer (needs the llm_* fields; without a key, !ask falls back to the fact engine), and the bot replies when addressed by one of chat_ai_names. Autonomous chimes are rare and only happen in light conversation; once chat_ai_busy_messages arrive inside chat_ai_busy_seconds the bot listens unless asked. A quiet-room opener can happen after chat_ai_quiet_seconds, but only once per human conversation lull - it never repeats on a timer into silence. chat_ai_chance is the odds per eligible light-chat moment, chat_ai_cooldown separates autonomous attempts, chat_ai_max_hour caps autonomous posts, and !cb off silences them. bot_personality empty = the built-in Doc voice.
_chat_ai_names: Words that address the bot in chat and get a reply. The bot's own nick (the "nick" field above) is ALWAYS a trigger too, automatically - with nick "TruckingWithDocBot", typing TruckingWithDocBot, doc or docbot all work. Matching is on word boundaries and case-insensitive, so 'doc' does not fire inside 'dockyard'.
_memory_db: The chat AI's memory (one SQLite file). While chat_ai_enabled is true, chat is logged (pruned after 90 days) and the bot distills durable per-viewer facts after it talks - work, pets, hobbies, plans, preferences. Health, politics, religion, finances and anything intimate are never kept. A moderator can erase a viewer entirely with !forget <viewer>.
_llm_no_think: Set true when llm_model is a Qwen3-family model running locally (qwen3:8b, qwen3:4b): appends Qwen3's /no_think switch to every prompt so the model answers directly instead of thinking first - on CPU, thinking turns a one-line chat reply into a half-minute stall.
_log_file: Set to a filename (e.g. "bot.log") and everything the console shows is also appended to that file - including crash tracebacks - so the log survives the window scrolling away. Watch it live with PowerShell: Get-Content .\bot.log -Wait. Empty = console only.
_persona_state_path: Where the mod-chosen voice (!persona set) is saved so it survives restarts. The bot's available voices: doc, sarge, rookie, rusty, nightshift, medic, cb, squaddie, coach, cowboy, flo, commentator, noir (or !persona custom <description>) - and whichever is active, it always knows the streamer's story.
_subgoal_state_path: Where the sub goal (!subgoal set <goal> <what happens when we hit it>) is saved. Twitch only lets the broadcaster's own token read live sub counts, so mods keep the number moving with !subgoal add/sub/count - anyone can check it with a bare !subgoal.
_subgoal_auto_count: true (the default): every sub, resub and gifted sub the bot SEES announced in chat bumps the sub goal on its own - the community-gift banner is skipped so gifts are never counted twice, and crossing the goal posts the payoff line. Anything the bot misses while offline is corrected with !subgoal count N. false: mods move the number entirely by hand.
